authority: independent iOS local Remote controller; not official recovered behavior
finding: An events/read started before an operation could replace HostState after the operation began; matching thread/cursor alone cannot reject it when a send keeps both unchanged. Late errors could also overwrite current connection status.
change: Per-host read generation invalidated on refresh/new-thread/send/cancel and leaving the screen. Both success and failure callbacks require current generation; success additionally requires unchanged thread/cursor and no task cancellation.
limits: Main-actor admission verified in isolated Swift tests, not device scheduling proof.
Existing Remote UI still lacks full thread catalog and official visual parity.
